coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 12
record.summary: Planned office/laboratory building on the Potrero Power Station masterplan, paired with Block 11 as a combined ~430,000 sq ft life-science campus; design under review as of the March 2025 annual compliance report, with no construction start found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land within the former power station site (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram via multi-point real-street georeferencing (see digitization_method), but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes. Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade. South edge corrected 2026-09-16 using the source diagram's own measured depth (see digitization_method) -- should be reliable to within a few meters, but has NOT been independently confirmed against a visible real-world curb. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 via GDAL GCP/TPS georeferencing -- see digitization_method. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third pass) in a single consistent pixel-detection pass across the whole block layout -- see digitization_method. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth pass) after fixing a mis-measured GCP -- see digitization_method.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Flat 100 ft max height per Figure 6.2.3. Paired with Block 11 in some secondary sources as a combined life-science campus (see that entry for the combined GSF estimate). No construction-start source found.

facts.value: Non-Retail Sales/Services (office) and Laboratory/Life Science uses permitted; Residential Not Permitted under the adopted D4D final Table 3.1.1 (a 2026 proposed DA amendment would add residential flexibility here -- see milestones)
flat 100 ft max per the D4D's Figure 6.2.3
Blocks 11 and 12 combined: approximately 430,000 sq ft of office, with below-grade parking, per the project's MEP engineer
Herzog & de Meuron + Adamson (Blocks 11, 12 and 15 together)
Seeking LEED Gold certification; designed as an all-electric building

Bus shelter and transit operator restroom delivered with Block 12, per the Phasing Table; a 100% Schematic Design plan set incorporating SFMTA/Public Works feedback was sent to those agencies January 7, 2022
Listed as part of Phase 1 in the 2024 annual compliance report ('Phase 1 includes Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, and 15...')

milestones.text: Board of Supervisors approves the Potrero Power Station project and Development Agreement (Ordinance No. 62-20, Board File 200040), the entitlement that first names Block 12 as a development block under the adopted Design for Development's Land Use Table; the Development Agreement's own effective date is May 25, 2020, distinct from the D4D's own February 26, 2020 final-document date. (Block 12 was later named one of Phase 1's six blocks by the October 2020 Phase 1 Development Phase Application -- a construction-phase assignment, not when it first entered the plan.)

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 12; the most recent primary source found (the 2024 annual compliance report) describes design as 'under review', not approved.

The combined 430,000 sq ft figure for Blocks 11+12 comes from the project's MEP engineer, not a Planning Department document; no Planning Commission or Planning Director approval memo for Block 12 was found to confirm or break out this figure.

The Chronicle's July 2026 report of a proposed +23 ft height increase and added residential flexibility is tied to a pending Development Agreement/Planning Code amendment (BOS Files 260724 and 260770) that had not been adopted as of this dossier's last-verified date.
